1.label: very_easy
1.summary: Two broad ledges, no decoy footholds, and a forgiving contact radius make the support transfer easy to read.
1.natural_language: Guide the brass walker out of the crater. Raise one leg, place it on the next visible ledge, lower it, and press SETTLE after each change. Keep at least three feet supported.

2.label: easy
2.summary: Three rising ledges add one extra transfer and one nearby false foothold while preserving wide contacts.
2.natural_language: Guide the brass walker out through three rising support terraces. Raise one leg, place it on the next ledge, lower it, and press SETTLE after each change. Keep at least three feet supported.

3.label: medium
3.summary: Four terraces alternate their lateral bias, requiring the next support to be inferred across depth.
3.natural_language: Climb the four-terrace crater route and escape. Use the yaw, lift, and extend controls to transfer one foot at a time; inspect the orbitable scene before SETTLE.

4.label: hard
4.summary: Five nonplanar terraces, three decoys, tighter contacts, and rotating transfer legs couple support and posture decisions.
4.natural_language: Escape the five-terrace crater with the brass walker. For every transfer, release the indicated support safely, tune that leg's yaw/lift/extend channels, lower it onto a real ledge, then SETTLE. Keep three feet supporting the body and read the 3D slope before committing.

5.label: very_hard
5.summary: Six narrow, laterally shifting terraces and five close decoys demand longer support planning with less contact slack.
5.natural_language: Find the six-terrace route out of the crater. Transfer support one leg at a time with yaw, lift, and extend, use the orbit view to resolve near and far ledges, and SETTLE only while the body remains upright on at least three contacts.

simplified.summary: Select a leg channel and nudge its signed yaw, lift, or extend value with visible plus and minus buttons; orbit with the view buttons.

full.summary: Drag the three signed actuator rails directly for the selected leg and drag the 3D viewport to orbit; SETTLE remains a visible action button.
